main_text.p: ea etiam, quæ ipse fieri simpliciter nolit, euenant: sicut, cum ipse ἀδικούμενος suos explorare constitutum habeat, eius administri τιμωρίαν infligant?

Secundò, errant & sibijpsis nimium blandiuntur, cum qualem animaduersionem peccata postulent, sese rectissimè intelligere putant, ac speciem afflictionum leuissimam sibijpsis decernunt: indignè interim ferentes, si secus quàm sitipsi ui sum, tractentur.

Postremò, nimium tribuunt potentiæ & licentiæ humanæ, cùm nullis metis diuinitùs eam coherceri, stultè opinantur. Item, cùm administris castigationis diuinæ sic irafcuntur, ac si abillis solis animaduersio profecta, & in ipsorum arbitrio posita esset.

Vt ex istorum errorum labyrinthis euadamus, firmiter nobis persuadeamus, nihil sine Patre cœlesti nobis euenire: minus, quàm pro malis nostris meritis, nobiscum agi: hostes piorum nihil nisi determinante & permittente Deo, efficere posse: denique, cùm Domino uiuamus & moriamur, nihil triste nobis accidere, etiamsi ad Domini gloriam, à scelestissimis

page.notes: The last line of the page reads "etiamsi ad Domini gloriam, à scelestissi-" continued as "mis" on the following line (the hyphenated word "scelestissimis" is split). Transcribed as printed. Several long-s forms rendered as plain s. Greek words in the text ("ἀδικούμενος", "τιμωρίαν") are read from the scan and are uncertain; marked not individually flagged, but the Greek in the first line is hard to read and should be checked. Printed hyphen at the line end after "scelestissi-" is kept as the word breaks across lines. Page is slightly skewed and the lower left corner is in shadow.
